<p><img alt="Mac mini vs Studio Feature" width="2000" height="1125" class="alignnone size-full wp-image-974499 lazyload" src="https://images.macrumors.com/images-new/1x1.trans.gif" data-src="https://images.macrumors.com/t/9l8DKXtl2XOimXxufEcehq1QXoE=/400x0/article-new/2024/10/Mac-mini-vs-Studio-Feature.jpg?lossy" data-srcset="https://images.macrumors.com/t/9l8DKXtl2XOimXxufEcehq1QXoE=/400x0/article-new/2024/10/Mac-mini-vs-Studio-Feature.jpg?lossy 400w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/CunE8BXY4omcCaOQnIPR-kjPKcI=/800x0/article-new/2024/10/Mac-mini-vs-Studio-Feature.jpg?lossy 800w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/GZXc5JPIF1lVV1LWnMGJ3vEssds=/1600x0/article-new/2024/10/Mac-mini-vs-Studio-Feature.jpg?lossy 1600w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/6wMrGzu4uIcZydYzCOf2TcGRUzY=/2500x0/filters:no_upscale()/article-new/2024/10/Mac-mini-vs-Studio-Feature.jpg?lossy 2500w" data-sizes="auto" loading="lazy" style="aspect-ratio:2000/1125"><noscript><img src="https://images.macrumors.com/article-new/2024/10/Mac-mini-vs-Studio-Feature.jpg" alt="Mac mini vs Studio Feature" width="2000" height="1125" class="alignnone size-full wp-image-974499"></noscript><br>There are now two desktop Macs to choose from following the discontinuation of the Mac Pro, but the prices have moved sharply. The ‌Mac Studio‌ starts at $2,499 and rises to $5,499 for the M5 Ultra model, while the ‌Mac mini‌ starts at $899 with the M6 chip and $1,699 with the M5 Pro.</p>
<p>Those prices come on top of the across-the-board Mac and <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/ipad/">iPad</a> increases Apple made in June, which took the ‌Mac mini‌ from $599 to $799, the M4 Pro configuration from $1,399 to $1,599, and the ‌Mac Studio‌ from $1,999 to $2,499. The M5 Ultra adds a further $200 to the post-June M3 Ultra price, putting it $1,500 above what the M3 Ultra cost at launch.</p>
<p>Our guide helps to answer the question of how to decide which of these two desktop Macs is best for you. The two machines now share a large number of key features, including:<br>
 </p>
<ul>
<li>A boxy silver aluminum enclosure with no color options</li>
<li>Apple's N1 chip, bringing Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 to both machines for the first time</li>
<li>Neural Accelerators built into every GPU core</li>
<li>Hardware-accelerated ray tracing</li>
<li>A Media Engine with hardware-accelerated H.264, HEVC, ProRes, and ProRes RAW, plus AV1 decode</li>
<li>A next-generation SSD architecture that Apple says is up to twice as fast as before</li>
<li><a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/08/26/new-mac-mini-and-mac-studio-add-genlock/">Genlock support over USB-C</a> for synchronizing a display with a camera, including the <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/iphone-17-pro/">iPhone 17 Pro</a></li>
<li>An HDMI port with multichannel audio output</li>
<li>A 3.5mm headphone jack with support for high-impedance headphones</li>
</ul>
<p>Beyond that, the two lines diverge on chip generation, memory capacity, ports, and external display support.</p>

<p>Most customers should choose the M5 Pro ‌Mac mini‌ over the M5 Max ‌Mac Studio‌, saving $800 on the base models. The gap widens across custom configurations, since the ‌Mac Studio‌'s memory and storage tiers start higher and climb further.</p>
<p>There is an unusual situation at the bottom of the lineup this year. The $899 ‌Mac mini‌ is the only machine of the four with a latest-generation chip, and the M6 is <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/08/25/apple-reveals-m6/">Apple's first 2nm chip</a>. Its Dual 16-core Neural Engine, which Apple says system frameworks can drive simultaneously, is also more Neural Engine hardware than either the M5 Pro or the M5 Max provides. If your workload leans on on-device machine learning rather than sustained CPU or GPU throughput, the cheapest Mac in this comparison is not obviously the weakest one for the task. The trade-offs are Thunderbolt 4 rather than Thunderbolt 5, a 32GB memory and 2TB storage ceiling, and a single video encode engine.</p>
<p>You should only consider the ‌Mac Studio‌ if you have a professional workflow that can genuinely leverage the M5 Max or the M5 Ultra, along with the additional ports, display outputs, and memory capacity. If you need the ‌Mac Studio‌, you will likely already know that you are looking for a highly powerful machine capable of supporting a specific intense workload. The <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/08/25/apple-debuts-m5-ultra/">M5 Ultra</a> is Apple's first quad-die M-series chip, and its four ProRes engines, four video encode engines, and 1.2TB/s of memory bandwidth are aimed squarely at multi-stream video work and large local AI models. The 512GB memory ceiling has no equivalent anywhere else in the Mac lineup, and it is what allows models with hundreds of billions of parameters to run entirely on device.</p>
<p>The ‌Mac Studio‌ still has a superior selection of ports, with four rear Thunderbolt 5 ports on the M5 Max and six in total on the M5 Ultra, plus an SDXC card slot, USB-A, and 10Gb Ethernet as standard. This makes a practical difference for anyone working off fast external storage or camera media. The ‌Mac mini‌ has closed part of the distance by moving to 2.5Gb Ethernet as standard, up from Gigabit.</p>
<p>Clustering over Thunderbolt 5 and RDMA is not a point of difference between the two machines, since it arrived in macOS 26.2 last December and works on any Mac with Thunderbolt 5, including the M5 Pro ‌Mac mini‌ and the previous-generation ‌Mac Studio‌. The exception is the M6 ‌Mac mini‌, which has Thunderbolt 4 and cannot take part.</p>
<p>Both ‌Mac mini‌ models still cap out at three external displays, but they now <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/08/26/new-mac-mini-bumps-display-refresh-rates/">reach 165Hz at 4K</a>, up from 144Hz on the M4 generation, and the M5 Pro model drives all three through a single Thunderbolt port. For a three-display desk setup at high refresh rates, the M5 Pro ‌Mac mini‌ is sufficient. It is only above three displays, or at 6K and 8K, that the ‌Mac Studio‌ becomes necessary.</p>
<p>A notable exception arises at the top of the ‌Mac mini‌ lineup. An M5 Pro ‌Mac mini‌ configured with additional memory and storage moves close enough to the $2,499 ‌Mac Studio‌ that the comparison changes somewhat. For an increment of a few hundred dollars, the ‌Mac Studio‌ substitutes a chip with roughly twice the memory bandwidth, a second video encode engine, far greater display support, and headroom to 128GB of unified memory. If you are already spending heavily on a ‌Mac mini‌, price the ‌Mac Studio‌ before committing.</p>
<p>If you plan to keep the machine for many years, the ‌Mac Studio‌'s ceiling matters more than its starting price, because it is the only one of the two that can be configured beyond 64GB of unified memory. Buyers weighing the M6 ‌Mac mini‌ against the M5 Pro ‌Mac mini‌ should note that the newer chip generation and the newer process node both sit in the cheaper machine, and that the M5 Pro's advantages are concentrated in multi-core and graphics performance rather than in longevity.</p>
<p>To some extent, purchasing decisions should be driven by budget, but any savings on the computer itself can be put toward a good external display such as Apple's <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/studio-display/">Studio Display</a>, which starts from $1,599 and was one of the few products spared June's price rises. An M6 ‌Mac mini‌ paired with a ‌Studio Display‌ comes to $2,498, a dollar less than a bare M5 Max ‌Mac Studio‌ with nothing to plug into. An M5 Pro ‌Mac mini‌ and a ‌Studio Display‌ together come to $3,298, which is $799 more than the base ‌Mac Studio‌ and $2,201 less than the M5 Ultra ‌Mac Studio‌ with no display at all.</p>

<p lang="en" dir="ltr">Great reporting from <a href="https://x.com/markgurman?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">@markgurman</a>. The new Dynamic Island with 3 items is already supported in iOS 27. Here's what it looks like.

 <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script></div><p></p>
<p>According to pdfu, the underlying code requires a sensor region less than 100 layout points wide to enable the new mode, or below 16.57mm. Layout points are Apple's device-independent unit for describing on-screen dimensions, and they scale differently depending on a display's resolution. By comparison, pdfu notes that the sensor region on the current <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/iphone-17-pro/">iPhone 17 Pro</a> measures 20.76mm, meaning Apple would need to shrink the hardware by roughly 20% to unlock the new software behavior.</p>
<p>The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max have been rumored to feature a smaller ‌Dynamic Island‌ for months, but reports about support for a third, additional ‌Dynamic Island‌ Live Activity is new. Since the iPhone 14 Pro launched in 2022, the ‌Dynamic Island‌ has only supported two Live Activities, so adding a third seems like a worthwhile way to demonstrate the utility of shrinking the region.</p>

<p><img alt="Four iPhone 18 Pro Colors Mock Feature" width="2500" height="1406" class="aligncenter size-full wp-image-1045343 lazyload" src="https://images.macrumors.com/images-new/1x1.trans.gif" data-src="https://images.macrumors.com/t/RpS_NbMfV5uA3pY-49XvA6SGQwo=/400x0/article-new/2026/04/Four-iPhone-18-Pro-Colors-Mock-Feature.jpg?lossy" data-srcset="https://images.macrumors.com/t/RpS_NbMfV5uA3pY-49XvA6SGQwo=/400x0/article-new/2026/04/Four-iPhone-18-Pro-Colors-Mock-Feature.jpg?lossy 400w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/6Ms6c62Jd2lZXrBLCvr2gXojP8E=/800x0/article-new/2026/04/Four-iPhone-18-Pro-Colors-Mock-Feature.jpg?lossy 800w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/eVxV9_YlUoSLrEN0-qRirlYcp3s=/1600x0/article-new/2026/04/Four-iPhone-18-Pro-Colors-Mock-Feature.jpg?lossy 1600w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/1MazXNDxLU5pD2u4VAtrAENsEmw=/2500x0/filters:no_upscale()/article-new/2026/04/Four-iPhone-18-Pro-Colors-Mock-Feature.jpg?lossy 2500w" data-sizes="auto" loading="lazy" style="aspect-ratio:2500/1406"><noscript><img src="https://images.macrumors.com/article-new/2026/04/Four-iPhone-18-Pro-Colors-Mock-Feature.jpg" alt="Four iPhone 18 Pro Colors Mock Feature" width="2500" height="1406" class="aligncenter size-full wp-image-1045343"></noscript><br>The findings apparently come from Apple's charging optimizer settings buried in ‌iOS 27‌, which show the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max charging at a rate 33% higher than the <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/iphone-17/">iPhone 17</a> lineup. If Apple can maintain that higher rate throughout a charge, pdfu estimates it could cut around 25% off the time it takes to complete a typical fast-charging session.</p>
<p>Apple's first foldable iPhone does not appear to get the same treatment. The same code purportedly shows it charging at the same rate as the ‌iPhone 17‌ and ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌, rather than the faster rate expected for the new Pro models.</p>
<p>The research also points to further charging improvements arriving with future models. The standard <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/iphone-18/">iPhone 18</a> is said to match the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ faster charging, while the iPhone 18e is said to see an even bigger jump of around 69% over the current <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/iphone-17e/">iPhone 17e</a>. The <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/iphone-air/">iPhone Air</a> 2 is said to charge about 27% faster than today's ‌iPhone Air‌.</p>
<p>Actual charging speeds depend on a multitude of real-world factors, such as the phone's temperature and how full the battery already is, so the improvement buyers notice day-to-day could end up being smaller than the numbers suggest.</p>
<p>Apple is expected to unveil the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, along with its first foldable iPhone, at its "Surprise and shine" event today, while the iPhone 18e, ‌iPhone 18‌, and ‌iPhone Air‌ 2 are rumored to follow in the spring of 2027.</p>

href="https://www.macrumors.com/author/hartley-charlton/" rel="author" class="authorLink--3Zlx7Owv">Hartley Charlton</a></div><div class="content--2u3grYDr js-content"><div class="ugc--2nTu61bm high-end iPhones by just $100 per model upon the announcement of the <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/roundup/iphone-18-pro/">iPhone 18 Pro</a> and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, <a href="https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-09/apple-event-details-2-000-iphone-duo-apple-watch-series-12-recording-feature"><em>Bloomberg</em>'s Mark Gurman</a> reports, which is a smaller bump than many had been bracing for ahead of today's event.</p>
<p><img alt="Apple Logo Cash Feature Mint" width="2676" height="1504" class="aligncenter size-full wp-image-834995 lazyload" src="https://images.macrumors.com/images-new/1x1.trans.gif" data-src="https://images.macrumors.com/t/AwbZC6x5cfeq97PncQMZilMeayU=/400x0/article-new/2022/01/Apple-Logo-Cash-Feature-Mint.jpg?lossy" data-srcset="https://images.macrumors.com/t/AwbZC6x5cfeq97PncQMZilMeayU=/400x0/article-new/2022/01/Apple-Logo-Cash-Feature-Mint.jpg?lossy 400w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/9wSsrXr8HaBDf7TRhRTLEkwFY0k=/800x0/article-new/2022/01/Apple-Logo-Cash-Feature-Mint.jpg?lossy 800w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/jIjiLoof0kexn53dr-1kPwG-PS0=/1600x0/article-new/2022/01/Apple-Logo-Cash-Feature-Mint.jpg?lossy 1600w,https://images.macrumors.com/t/HleQ7Y0q8sD4f_X1s8CDGhVKEJA=/2500x0/filters:no_upscale()/article-new/2022/01/Apple-Logo-Cash-Feature-Mint.jpg?lossy 2500w" data-sizes="auto" loading="lazy" style="aspect-ratio:2676/1504"><noscript><img src="https://images.macrumors.com/article-new/2022/01/Apple-Logo-Cash-Feature-Mint.jpg" alt="Apple Logo Cash Feature Mint" width="2676" height="1504" class="aligncenter size-full wp-image-834995"></noscript><br>In June, Apple <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/06/25/apple-just-increased-prices/">hiked the cost</a> of all of its Macs, iPads, and home products in response to the global memory shortage, but chose to keep iPhone pricing intact at the time. That is widely expected to change today, with the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max expected to come in at a higher price than their predecessors.</p>
<p>Gurman's $100 figure comes in well below some of the more dire predictions floated over the summer. Analytics firm IDC had <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/06/26/iphone-18-pro-price-increase-estimate/">suggested increases of up to $200</a> for the Pro models, while GF Securities analyst Jeff Pu warned costs for the A20 Pro chip, RAM, and storage could <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/07/31/iphone-18-pro-models-300-more-expensive/">push prices as much as $300 higher</a>. TrendForce, citing memory chip costs that have risen nearly 400% year-on-year, had also <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/09/03/iphone-18-pro-prices-apple-event-next-week/">modeled a $150 to $200 jump</a>. Apple appears to be absorbing more of that cost itself rather than passing all of it on to buyers.</p>
<p>Earlier this year, Apple took steps to soften the blow of rising prices by launching the <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/07/28/apple-upgrade-program-klarna/">Apple Upgrade</a> program in the U.S. The Klarna-backed leasing plan allows customers to pay a monthly fee in perpetuity and swap their device out annually for the newest version. Wireless carriers could also help to ease iPhone "sticker shock" by offering aggressive installment plans and trade-in incentives, Gurman added.</p>

<p>Previously, the Dynamic Island could only display up to two Live Activities at a time. This design has been in place since the iPhone 14 Pro and iPhone 14 Pro Max, which launched in 2022.</p>
<p>Otherwise, Gurman says the look of the iPhone 18 Pro models is similar to the iPhone 17 Pro models, save for a new "burgundy red" color option replacing the popular Cosmic Orange. Sky blue and Silver have also been <a href="https://www.macrumors.com/2026/09/02/leaked-iphone-18-pro-parts-point-to-three-colors/">reported previously</a> as potential color options.</p>
<p>Internal upgrades include a new A20 Pro chip manufactured using TSMC's 2nm process, longer battery life, a revamped vapor chamber cooling system, and a mechanical aperture lens that enables more precise depth of field and better low-light performance – though this latter feature may be exclusive to the larger iPhone 18 Pro Max.</p>
<p>Apple's "<a href="https://www.macrumors.com/guide/apple-september-2026-what-to-expect/">Surprise and Shine</a>" event kicks off at 10:00 a.m. Pacific Time later today, and we'll have full coverage right here on <em>MacRumors</em>.</p>
